name: How can I make my kitchen accessible for someone using a wheelchair?
description: For wheelchair accessibility, widen doorways, ensure clear floor space, lower countertops/sinks, and install pull-out storage.

mainEntity.name: How can I make my kitchen accessible for someone using a wheelchair?

acceptedAnswer.text: To make a kitchen accessible for wheelchair users, key modifications include widening doorways to at least 32 inches, ensuring adequate clear floor space (a 60-inch turning radius is ideal), lowering countertops and sinks to a height of 28-34 inches with clear knee space underneath, and installing pull-out shelves or drawers for easier reach. Additionally, consider side-opening ovens and roll-under cooktops. Hometelligent Inc. designs solutions that integrate these features seamlessly while adhering to ADA guidelines where applicable.
